text:
elena: heads-up — seeing a spike of 503s from hosted inference starting ~09:12 UTC. Several customers report timeouts followed by upstream 503s. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/errors (pool-7, model: rdx-small-v2)

oncall-sre: looking now, pulling logs from pool-7 instances.

deploy-bot: [09:18 UTC] autoscaler: pool-7 desired=12 -> actual=14 (scale up triggered).

ashwin: grabbing runner logs — lots of repeated SIGBUS / page fault traces, then container OOM-kill/restart. attaching snippet:
```
[runner] 2026-03-15T09:16:03Z ERROR illegal memory access at 0x7ff... qkv_prefetch.cu: line 482
[runner] 2026-03-15T09:16:03Z FATAL cuMemAlloc returned CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[kernel] 2026-03-15T09:16:03Z SIGBUS at 0x7ffaa3 (stacktrace: qkv_kernel+0x1f4)
```

samir: impact estimate: rolling 3% error rate across hosted region us-west-2, customers: acme-inc, beta-apps. Support tickets coming in.

elena: any immediate mitigation? Can we route affected routes to dedicated or smaller model?

oncall-sre: enabled fallback to rdx-tiny for rdx-small-v2 for traffic from tier=free (will reduce accuracy). Also increased eviction threshold on pool-7 to avoid noisy restarts.

ashwin: repro steps I ran: large batch (batch_size=64) with long sequence (>2048) and kv-prefetch enabled triggers large transient cuMemAlloc requests during prefetch window which sometimes fail on these kernels, then subsequent page faults on warm memory pages. Workaround locally: disable kv-prefetch or reduce batch_size.

support-lead: filed TKT-83021 with customer details and notified acct team. They reported sequence of latency spikes before the 503s.

samir: hypothesis: a recent host-level NVIDIA driver update plus our kv-prefetch path exposes stale GPU memory/migration edge-case causing SIGBUS on qkv prefetch. Repro'd on 2 of 6 nodes in the pool.

elena: next steps: collect core dumps & gpu diagnostics from affected nodes, disable kv-prefetch cluster-side for pool-7, and consider rolling back driver on repro hosts. Who owns host driver rollbacks?

ashwin: I'll collect cores (/var/crash/*runner*.core), nv-crash logs and dmesg. Pushing a hot patch to disable kv-prefetch on pool-7 at 09:37 UTC. Also throttling max_batch_size to 32. Planning driver rollback if errors persist.

oncall-sre: mitigation applied: kv-prefetch Disabled on pool-7 @09:37 UTC, max_batch_size set to 32. Error rate down to 0.4% as of 09:52 UTC. Monitoring.

deploy-bot: [09:45 UTC] pool-7: rollback-flag=kprefetch=false applied to all 14 instances; restart rolling.

elena: leaving monitoring on for 30m; if stable we'll open a postmortem to track follow-up (driver backout, add prefetch safety checks).

support-lead: customers notified of temporary fallback; will update tickets after stability window.

ashwin: collecting artifacts and will open infra bug (INFRA-1129) with kernel traces + repro.

elena: thanks team — tagging @oncall for postmortem owner.
